title: adaptive-route-token-bundles-prd-2026-05
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Summary:

This PRD describes Adaptive Route Token Bundles (ARTB), a product initiative to let customers buy, assign, and manage token bundles that are scoped to a specific route (or set of routes). ARTB targets two customer needs: predictable unit economics for high-volume routes, and controlled burst capacity without manual intervention. The feature covers purchase flows, per-route assignment, auto-topup, billing treatment, Console/UI controls, API surfaces, and telemetry requirements.

Context and motivating problems:
- Teams running production LLM features (recommendations, search, chat support flows) want cheaper predictable units for sustained heavy usage rather than pay-as-you-go variability.
- Platform and finance teams need guardrails for bursty routes (embeddings, vectorization jobs) to avoid surprise bills.
- Dedicated customers require on-contract pricing constructs and audit trails for route-level spending.

Goals:
- G1: Enable customers to purchase token bundles (named bundles) and assign them to one or more routes with clear billing visibility.
- G2: Support automatic topups when a bundle dips below a threshold with configurable topup methods (prepaid charge, invoice hold, or disable topup).
- G3: Provide per-route consumption accounting, real-time bundle usage dashboards, and alerting for low-balance and over-consumption.
- G4: Ensure compatibility with Dedicated, Hosted, and Private deployments (with reasonable limitations for air-gapped environments).

Success metrics (30/60/90 days post-launch):
- Adoption: 25% of new Dedicated customers assign at least one token bundle within 60 days.
- Spend predictability: Average month-to-month variance in per-route spend for bundle-backed routes drops by 40% for adopters.
- Customer satisfaction: CSAT for billing related inquiries decreases by 20% for customers using ARTB.
- Operational: Billing disputes related to burst tokens decrease by 50% for customers on ARTB.

Must-have requirements:
- R1: Purchase API and Console flow to create a token bundle with parameters: name, token_count, effective_start, effective_end (optional), price_plan_reference, auto_topup_policy.
- R2: Route assignment API: assign/unassign bundle_id to route_id(s), with validation that the caller has route.admin permission.
- R3: Real-time accounting: every routed token consumption must decrement the assigned bundle in near-real-time (<5s propagation to UI).
- R4: Auto-topup policies: support three modes: prepaid_charge (instant charge to payment method), invoice_on_cycle (defer to next billing cycle), and topup_disabled (stop serving when depleted).
- R5: Billing integration: bundle usage must be reflected in monthly invoices with line-item granularity: bundle_purchase, topup_events, overage_charges.
- R6: Audit logs: purchases, assignments, auto-topups, and overage events must emit audit entries that include actor_id, route_id, bundle_id, tokens_consumed, and timestamp.

Nice-to-have requirements:
- N1: Bundle sharing: ability to share a bundle across multiple routes with consumption weighting rules.
- N2: Per-route priority class that consumes from bundle first, then falls back to pay-as-you-go.
- N3: Console visualization of projected exhaustion date given recent consumption patterns.

Non-goals / explicitly out of scope:
- Long-term credit trading or marketplace for bundles between customers.
- Fine-grained token-level reservation for single-request pinning.

User journeys:
- Purchase & assign (admin): In Console, Billing -> Token Bundles -> Create Bundle -> enter token count and pricing plan -> choose auto-topup -> Create. Then navigate to Routes -> select route -> Assign Bundle -> choose bundle_id and priority -> Save.
- Auto-topup flow (prepaid_charge): When bundle balance < topup_threshold, billing-service charges saved payment method, creates topup_event, and increases bundle balance. Audit log emitted.
- Depleted bundle with topup_disabled: When balance reaches zero, route-level behavior follows config: either reject requests (HTTP 402) or fall back to pay-as-you-go if configured. System emits RouteCostCapExceeded alert.

High-level design notes:
- Data model additions:
  - token_bundles table: bundle_id (UUID), name, owner_org_id, tokens_total, tokens_available, price_plan_ref, auto_topup_policy, topup_threshold, created_at, expires_at
  - route_bundle_assignments: route_id, bundle_id, priority, assigned_at

- Billing model and pricing behavior:
  - Bundles are sold as pre-sized token packs with a configured price_plan_ref which maps to per-token amortized price and revenue recognition rules.
  - Auto-topup prepaid_charge applies standard per-token rate for the purchased topup, not the bundle amortized rate unless the customer selects a matching promo.
  - When both a bundle and pay-as-you-go are enabled, bundle tokens are consumed first according to assignment priority.
  - Overages (consumption when bundle exhausted and topup not available) billed at standard pay-as-you-go rates and flagged for dispute if configured.

- Consumption path (runtime):
  - routing-proxy attaches route_id to each request. At token emission, a token-accounting service checks route_bundle_assignments in-memory cache, decrements tokens_available using an optimistic concurrency update, emits usage_event, and returns billing_token_id to runtime for invoice correlation.
  - For high-throughput routes, we support chunked attribution: runtime requests a token-reservation batch (n tokens) to reduce per-token RPCs. Reservations expire in 30s if not consumed.

APIs and CLI:
- POST /v1/bundles {name, tokens_total, price_plan_ref, auto_topup_policy, topup_threshold, expires_at}
- POST /v1/routes/{route_id}/bundle-assign {bundle_id, priority}
- GET /v1/bundles/{bundle_id}/usage
- CLI examples: redwood bundles create --name "search-bulk-1" --tokens 1000000 --price-plan enterprise-2026 --auto-topup prepaid_charge --topup-threshold 0.15

Console UX / product surface:
- Billing -> Token Bundles: list view with balances, projected exhaustion, linked routes, recent topup events.
- Route Settings: assign/unassign bundle, set consumption priority, set depletion behavior (deny or fallback to pay-as-you-go).
- Alerts: prebuilt alert template BundleLowBalance and BundleTopupFailed.

Telemetry and observability:
- New metrics: bundle_tokens_available (gauge, tagged by bundle_id), bundle_tokens_consumed_total (counter), bundle_topup_events_total (counter), bundle_reservation_failures (counter).
- Logs: bundle_audit_event containing actor_id, action, bundle_id, delta_tokens, route_id, request_ids (when applicable).
- Dashboards: Bundle Health (per-bundle: balance, 7-day burn rate, projected exhaustion), Route-Bundle Correlation.

Data and consistency guarantees:
- Consistency: tokens_available is strongly consistent for assignment and reservation operations. We use a leader-sharded token accounting service per org to avoid cross-DC races.
- Performance: bulk reservation path supports up to 10k tokens reservation per RPC. Per-token debit operations optimized with batched writes to ledger.

Compatibility and deployment considerations:
- Hosted: full feature set including auto-topup prepaid_charge.
- Dedicated: full feature set with contractual price_plan_refs; finance must provision price keys per customer.
- Private: auto-topup prepaid_charge disabled by default for air-gapped installs; topup_invoiced_on_cycle supported. Manual billing hooks required.

Security and compliance:
- Only users with billing.admin or route.admin can create/assign bundles.
- Bundle events must be retained for 2 years for audit purposes.
- Sensitive billing operations (prepaid charging) require 2FA for the initiating user in Console.

Migration plan for existing customers:
1. Offer an opt-in migration for high-spend routes: export existing monthly usage summary and generate suggested bundle sizes (Console wizard).
2. Pilot with 10 existing Dedicated customers for 6 weeks. Learn pricing acceptance and topup defaults.
3. Provide a bulk-assign CLI to map bundles to routes for customers with many routes.

Rollout plan and release gates:
- Phase 1 (internal + 5 pilot customers): API + Billing integration + Console list view. Pass gate: accurate near-real-time balancing (<5s) and successful topup charging in sandbox.
- Phase 2 (Beta): +25 customers, add reservation path and projected exhaustion UI. Pass gate: no regressions in billing reports and <1% reservation failure rate.
- Phase 3 (GA): general availability for Hosted and Dedicated, Private on request.

Safety checks & failure modes:
- Topup charge failure: emit BundleTopupFailed alert, fall back to invoice_on_cycle if configured, or set route to depletion_behavior as defined.
- Reservation expiration: tokens reserved but not consumed return to bundle; high expiration rates surface on dashboard.
- Under-billing risk: reconcile daily ledger dumps between token-accounting service and billing-service; discrepancies >0.1% trigger automatic investigation.

Open questions for product decisions:
- Q1: Should we allow peer-to-peer bundle transfers between orgs (currently set to No)?
- Q2: Discounting policy for auto-topup amounts vs initial bundle purchase (do we allow promo-consistent topups?): Finance to advise.
- Q3: Default topup_threshold percentage and whether it should be configurable per-org or per-bundle?

Dependencies:
- Billing-service: invoice line-item support and topup charging endpoint.
- Routing-proxy & token-accounting service: fast path integration for reservations.
- Console: Billing UI and Route assignment panel updates.
- Finance & Legal: price_plan_ref creation and revenue recognition guidance.

Ownership and stakeholders:
- Product: Sofia Martinez (owner)
- Engineering lead: Marco Silva (eng-serving-runtime)
- Billing & Finance: Alexis Nguyen (finance-and-legal)
- DX/SDKs: Evan Cho (eng-developer-experience)
- SRE: Priya Raman (eng-sre)
- Security & Compliance: Omar Haddad (security-and-compliance)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Unexpected billing disputes due to asynchronous accounting. Mitigation: strong consistency for token debits and daily ledger reconciliation.
- Risk: Customer confusion around pricing differences between bundle amortized rate and topup rate. Mitigation: Console explanations and pre-purchase simulator.
